title: Crestview Insurance onprem migration - TF module notes & capacity roadmap (draft)
content:
Summary:

This is an internal draft for the Crestview Insurance on-prem migration: a 3-phase plan to move their LLM inference workload into a customer-managed private deployment (VPC + on-prem GPU cluster). Document covers high-level capacity assumptions, Terraform module notes, upgrade/migration roadmap and an architecture Q&A. Intended audience: infra eng, solutions eng, platform security, and customer infra contacts.

Primary goals:
- Deliver a private Redwood control plane fronted by a secure VPC peering and VPN to Crestview’s datacenter.
- Guarantee 150 qps of small-text (<=256 tokens) inference at p99 <= 120ms for p95 requests during peak with burst headroom to 300 qps.
- Provide deterministic cost/ops guidance and a tested TF module set for onprem provisioning + network/iam integrations.

Assumptions (customer-provided / validated):
- Crestview will host 4 x DGX-A100 equivalent nodes (8x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs total) in their on-prem cluster in Rack A.
- Average inference request size: 120 tokens output, 80 tokens input. Token compute profile aligns with gpt-like decoder-only models.
- Concurrent active sessions target: 250 sessions, with average requests per second across sessions = 0.6 (=> 150 sustained qps).
- Storage: 5 TB for model artifacts + 2 TB for KV cache persistence across restarts.
- Network: 10 Gbps fabric between serving nodes, 1 Gbps egress to control plane.
- Security: Customer KMS (Vault/HSM) is available; Redwood must integrate via provided endpoints.

Sizing rationale (back-of-envelope):
- Model choice: crest-7b-quant (7B fp16-quantized profile) estimated throughput ~ 45 tokens/s per A100-80GB instance under Redwood runtime with batching optimizations.
- Per-request tokens = 200 combined input+output. For 150 qps -> 30k tokens/s.
- Required sustained token throughput across cluster = 30k tokens/s. At 45 tokens/s per GPU -> ~667 GPU-seconds/s -> implies ~15 GPUs if naive, but with batching/parallelism runtime yields 3x improvements for small requests. We therefore target 6-8 GPUs active with autoscaling buffers.
- Proposed initial GPU footprint: 8 GPUs (2 nodes x 4 GPUs) dedicated to production serving, reserve remaining 6 GPUs for canary, dev, and capacity buffer.
- CPU/RAM per serving node: 48 vCPU, 384 GB RAM to host runtime containers, KV cache and sidecars.

Terraform module notes (compatibility + changes):
- Module layout suggested for customer repo:
  - modules/network (vpc, subnets, routing, peering, firewall)
  - modules/compute (k8s nodegroups / vm-pools; gpu-machine-profiles)
  - modules/secret (kms integration + vault auth roles)
  - modules/deploy (redwood-agent, operators, service accounts)
  - modules/monitoring (prometheus, alertmanager, opentelemetry collectors)

- Key TF provider versions: aws v4.x for cloud pieces (if used for hybrid), kubernetes provider v3.x, hashicorp/vault v3.x. If Crestview uses onprem OpenStack/VMware, we will use the appropriate provider and push minimal changes to modules/compute.
- State strategy: keep shared state for network and secrets in remote backend (S3-compatible or internal object store + Dynamo-style locking) with separate workspaces per environment (prod/stage/canary).
- Module inputs of note:
  - compute.gpu_type 
  - compute.gpu_count_total
  - network.allowed_control_plane_cidrs (must allow Redwood control plane egress + customer management IPs)
  - secret.kms_key_id

- Upgrade/migration TF steps (high level):
  1) Freeze infra baseline: tag current TF state and export plan for existing cluster.
  2) Deploy network module to create peering/vpn and firewall rules. Run smoke test (ICMP/TCP to control-plane endpoints).
  3) Deploy compute module with node labels for redwood-role=canary. Install Redwood agent in canary mode.
  4) Gradually scale redwood-service to production node group, validate latency on canary subset, increment traffic via routing policy.
  5) Remove temporary canary labels/scale down dev buffer after steady-state.

Compatibility notes and breaking changes to watch for:
- TF 1.6 provider changes around the kubernetes provider resource ordering may require splitting module apply into two steps (CRDs first, then controllers).
- Vault auto-auth approach: older vault provider versions require extra service-account bootstrap; we recommend adding a bootstrap script to create approle roles if vault is air-gapped.
- If customer uses strict egress filtering, ensure we produce an allow-list for Redwood’s control plane IPs and telemetry endpoints before attempting agent registration.

KMS & secrets integration:
- Crestview prefers HSM-backed KMS (Thales/equivalent). We will design module/secret to accept a key identifier and use Vault transit for signing/encryption where possible.
- Secrets flow: Redwood operator stores ephemeral tokens in Vault; long-lived keys remain in customer KMS. We will avoid moving keys out of customer boundary.

Architecture Q&A (recorded exchanges with Crestview infra):
Q: Can Redwood run entirely offline (air-gapped) for inference traffic?
A: No—control plane requires occasional connectivity for management, rollout and usage telemetry. However, we support a limited offline mode for inference-only traffic if the control plane is reachable via maintenance windows.

Q: How will failover between onprem racks work?
A: Use k8s topology-aware scheduling + pod anti-affinity and dual-node-groups across racks. If a rack fails, autoscaler replaces capacity in surviving racks. Persistent KV cache uses replicated storage; recommend a multi-AZ-like replication across customer racks.

Q: What's the recommended quantization to reduce GPU memory needs?
A: 4-bit symmetric quantization (Q4) yields 2.5-3x memory reduction for the crest-7b model and preserves quality for our workloads. Add fallback to fp16 for regeneration-critical requests.

Open decisions & unknowns (action items):
- [A1] Confirm exact GPU model and PCIe fabric topology (edge-case: NVLink pooling between nodes changes memory-sharing assumptions). Owner: Crestview infra.
- [A2] Customer to provide KMS endpoint + CA bundle for Vault integration. Owner: Crestview security.
- [A3] Confirm acceptable telemetry endpoints / allow-list for security review. Owner: Redwood security.
- [A4] Agree on SLOs for canary phase and definition of readiness for cutover. Owner: Solutions Eng + Customer PM.

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Risk: Network egress blocking agent registration -> Mitigation: Provide pre-signed registration token + out-of-band config step with customer VPN.
- Risk: Underprovisioned KV cache causing p99 spikes -> Mitigation: Start with persistent SSD-backed cache + monitoring for miss-rate; enable autosized cache group.
- Risk: Terraform provider upgrade failure in staging -> Mitigation: Use a dedicated upgrade branch, stepwise apply, and keep older provider version as rollback path.

Minimal runbook for initial cutover (reference steps for on-call):
1) Pre-flight checklist (48h): confirm backup of TF state, network peering test, KMS access test, model artifacts present in object store.
2) Day 0 deploy (0-4h): apply network + vault modules, create node groups with canary label, deploy agent in canary.
3) Validation (4-12h): run synthetic load against canary endpoints (10% of traffic) and confirm p95/p99 within acceptance.
4) Progressive ramp (12-36h): route 25% -> 50% -> 100% traffic across 3 windows with post-step validation.
5) Post-cutover (36-72h): increase monitoring retention, capture baseline metrics, schedule a retro.

TF snippet examples (to be included in module repo):
- compute module input example:
  compute = {
    gpu_type = "a100-80gb"
    gpu_count_total = 8
    node_labels = { redwood-role = "prod" }
  }

- network module example inputs:
  network = {
    allowed_control_plane_cidrs = ["34.82.12.0/24", "34.82.13.0/24"]
    vpn_endpoint = "vpn.crestview.example.com"
  }

Checklist of artifacts to deliver for next milestone (M1):
- TF module PR with network + compute + secret modules (branch: crestview/m1).
- Integration test harness that exercises canary deployment via synthetic load.
- Runbook doc with exact CLI commands for rollback.
- Security review appendix with telemetry allow-list and KMS integration notes.

Notes to self / loose thoughts (informal):
- Consider offering a prebuilt OVA for customers who want single package install (less TF work but more ops).
- Explore moving some KV cache to a small Redis cluster on customer infra to simplify node restarts.
- Potential perf win by co-locating NVMe for model mmap. Need to confirm IO profile.

Appendix: rough cost buckets (internal estimate)
- Onprem engineering advisory: 6 weeks of SE time (0.5 FTE) for cutover and testing.
- Terraform & automation work: 3 sprints for module updates and CI.
- Ongoing support: standard Private Plan + 24x7 optionally add SRE on-call.

End of draft. Please add comments inline and call out any incorrect assumptions.
